mechanisms.behavior: The physical trough uses switches 18-21 from left to right plus jam opto 22. The proven Pro table creates four balls on 18-21. Output 1 ejects the rightmost ball and the script briefly drives switch 22 as the ball enters the shooter path.
mechanisms.label: Four-ball trough

mechanisms.behavior: Output 2 launches a ball held at shooter-lane switch 23. The proven Pro table uses direction 40 degrees, base power 40, random variation 0.3, and a 0.6 second full-plunge time.
mechanisms.label: Auto launcher

mechanisms.behavior: Switch 10 remains active while a ball is captured. Output 6 ejects it at 184 degrees with force 22, Z velocity 55, and angle/force variation 2 in the proven table.
mechanisms.label: Left eject

mechanisms.behavior: Ball impact drops the target and activates switch 11. Output 4 raises it and output 5 lowers it; raising it also releases a ball held behind the target.
mechanisms.label: Center memory drop target

mechanisms.behavior: Output 3 controls the center lock magnet. The proven table models a radius-55 grab field with centered capture and uses optos 33/34 for the bottom/top lock positions.
mechanisms.label: Center magnet lock

mechanisms.behavior: The Pro ship is a passive bash/shake toy above the center target, not the Premium/LE motorized dive assembly. A hit on switch 11 drops the target and shakes the ship. While output 7 is enabled, the Vengeance kicker returns a captured ball at 175 degrees and force 40. Do not add the Premium actuator, latch, crash opto, orbit gates, rotating VUK, or bottom-drain kickback.
mechanisms.label: Passive Vengeance bash toy and kickback

mechanisms.behavior: Physical outputs 15/16 drive the lower left/right flippers from dedicated buttons 84/82 and normally-closed EOS contacts 83/81. Physical output 12 and public D15 switch 86 operate the upper-right flipper. The proven legacy VPX table instead couples the visual upper flipper to output 16 and writes public switch 90; that is a table simplification, not the service wiring.
mechanisms.label: Three flippers

mechanisms.behavior: Switches 30/31/32 pulse outputs 9/10/11 for the left, right, and bottom pop bumpers.
mechanisms.label: Three pop bumpers

mechanisms.behavior: Each full spinner rotation pulses switch 12; there is no controller-facing actuator.
mechanisms.label: Spinner

mechanisms.behavior: The three independent standups pulse switches 1, 2, and 4 and correspond to the three BEAM ME UP insert words at lamps 65-67.
mechanisms.label: BEAM ME UP three-target bank

mechanisms.behavior: The four independent standups pulse switches 24, 25, 28, and 29 and correspond to lamps 4, 5, 7, and 8.
mechanisms.label: TREK four-target bank

mechanisms.behavior: The top, center, and bottom targets pulse switches 7, 8, and 9; matching inserts are lamps 74, 75, and 76.
mechanisms.label: Right three-target bank

mechanisms.behavior: The top, center, and bottom targets pulse switches 39, 40, and 41. Their physical inserts are lamps 55, 54, and 53 respectively; output 27 is the bank flasher.
mechanisms.label: Center three-target bank

mechanisms.behavior: The top and bottom targets pulse switches 42 and 43; their inserts are lamps 48 and 40.
mechanisms.label: Left two-target bank

mechanisms.behavior: Six independent red standups pulse switches 45-50 and correspond in order to lamps 50, 57, 59, 60, 68, and 69.
mechanisms.label: Six red standup targets

mechanisms.behavior: Warp-ramp optos are 13/36, left-ramp optos 14/35, and right-ramp optos 37/38. Left and right orbit switches are 52/51. Outputs 19/20 flash the ramp tops and outputs 23/28/29 flash the left ramp, right ramp, and left loop.
mechanisms.label: Ramps and orbits

mechanisms.behavior: Output 22 drives the unsensed playfield laser-projector motor.
mechanisms.label: Laser projector

mechanisms.behavior: Output 8 drives the optional cabinet shaker; an author may omit the physical accessory while retaining the controller binding.
mechanisms.label: Optional shaker
